rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OptionValue`.

**Nested arrays and maps.** `all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/config.rs` deserializes configs whose options hold a map inside a map (`nested`, `reasoning`) and an array inside a map (`array`). It asserts that `serde_json::to_value` returns the same JSON. It also round-trips through a string and compares the two configs, which exercises `Deserialize`, `Serialize` and `PartialEq`.

**Scalar types retained.** The same test covers a string (`"x"`, `"high"`), a bool (`true`), an integer (`1024`, `2`) and floats (`0.5`). Equality of the JSON values means an integer that came back as a float, or the reverse, would fail the comparison. `option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic` also asserts that JSON `1` deserializes to `OptionValue::Integer(1)` and JSON `1.0` to `OptionValue::Float(1.0)`. That is the distinction an untagged enum could get wrong.

**Floats must be finite when building a request.** The same test checks two cases:
- `OptionValue::Map` containing a nested `Float(INFINITY)` makes `validate()` return an error.
- An Ollama config with `Array[Float(NAN)]` makes `AgentConfig::options_json()` return an error. That is the request-building path, and it validates through nested arrays.

Both the array and map recursion branches are therefore exercised. `options_json` runs the same validation for every backend, so a separate non-finite test per backend would not check anything different.

**Trait implementations and `#[non_exhaustive]`.** `Clone`, `Debug`, `PartialEq`, `Serialize` and `Deserialize` are all derived. `Clone` and `Debug` are plain derives with no conditional or transformation of their own. The other three are exercised by the tests above. The `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute is a compile-time declaration with no runtime behavior to assert. `public_exports_match_the_appendix` in `tests/public_api.rs` checks the public API inventory.

I read the implementation only to confirm that the derives are plain and that `validate` is the finiteness check. I derived the expected behavior from the requirement text. I found no unacknowledged gap and no marking gap. All three tests carry `{test}` references to `OptionValue`.

text: An inference option may contain nested arrays and maps. Scalars retain their value types when serialized. Floating-point options must be finite when building a backend request.
Downstream callers matching on individual variants must include a fallback arm for future variants.
